# When predictive information admits positive dynamics

29 October 2026, Brisbane. Root construction. A short predictive record need not identify, or admit, a short underlying physical dynamics. The ordinary proof of the central transportation criterion and independent exact controls are preserved in `acquisition_frontier/DIRECTED_REALIZABILITY_TRANSPORT_REVIEW.md`. This root note develops its consequence interface, synthesis, and limits.

## 1. The new object and characterization

An oriented sufficient mean record on m labelled ports is
(S,w_B,b_R,b_L,c). S is an irreducible Eulerian Laplacian, w_B>0 are
calibrated port weights, and v_R=b_R-w_B, v_L=b_L-w_B are nonnegative
vectors with the same total V. For i!=j let F_ij=-S_ij. Set

    T={M>=0: M1=v_R, M^T1=v_L,
       M_ij=0 if i!=j and F_ij=0},
    J_*=min_{M in T} sum_{i!=j:F_ij>0} M_ij^2/F_ij.

Diagonal entries are allowed and unpenalized. For V>0, **a finite
irreducible positive CTMC realizes the record if and only if T is
nonempty and 2c>J_*.** Positive means nonnegative rates and positive
stationary weights, not strictly positive rates between every pair.
For V=0, c must be zero and the direct port chain suffices. Native port
holding rates are free design variables in this theorem.

Every realization using k hidden states satisfies

    2c >= (1+1/k)J_*,
    k >= J_*/(2c-J_*)  when J_*>0.

The proof identifies M as stationary hidden residence population jointly
labelled by entrance and exit port. Actual endpoint flux F and duration
sigma obey M_ij=F_ij E[sigma|i,j], row(M)=v_R, column(M)=v_L, and
sum F_ij E[sigma^2|i,j]=2c. A classical phase-type variance inequality
gives necessity. For sufficiency, choose an optimal transport, finite
diagonal return flux, and directed Erlang channels with the required
occupation masses; one explicit phase mixture adjusts the remaining
second moment. The complete proof covers arbitrary hidden cycles,
mixed entrance laws, and direct jumps with zero interior duration.

This is a **stationary network completion theorem for an incomplete
excursion-moment record**. Convex transport, scalar phase fitting and
Schur elimination remain conventional machinery. The proposed addition
is the exact equivalence between the stationary hidden-network problem
and this finite convex threshold. The targeted literature check found

# Positive predictive completion with finite clock ceilings

29 October 2026, Brisbane. Root's next attack after the unrestricted-clock
transport theorem. Mathematical input is an exact calibrated oriented
mean record. This theorem pays a substantive execution constraint:
prescribed ceilings on native state-changing departure rates.

## 1. The exact criterion

Use the notation of `POSITIVE_PREDICTIVE_REALIZATION.md`: an irreducible
Eulerian port Laplacian S, positive port weights w_B, nonnegative hidden
loads v_R,v_L with equal total V>0, and scalar c. Let F_ij=-S_ij for
i!=j and d_i=sum_{j!=i}F_ij. Prescribe a finite positive hidden-state
rate ceiling Lambda and positive port ceilings ell_i. These are upper
bounds, not fixed native holding rates.

There is first an unavoidable port budget:

    a_i=w_B,i ell_i-d_i >= 0.                           (1)

Define T_a as the nonnegative transportation matrices with row sums v_R
and column sums v_L, off-diagonal support restricted to F_ij>0, and
M_ii=0 whenever a_i=0. Positive diagonal transport is otherwise allowed.

For x>=0, f>0, write u=Lambda*x/f and n=floor(u), and define

    psi_Lambda(x,f)=f(n+1)(2u-n)/Lambda^2
      =max_{n in {0,1,...}}
        [2(n+1)x/Lambda-n(n+1)f/Lambda^2].              (2)

Set psi(0,0)=0 and psi(x,0)=infinity for x>0. Let

    J_cap=min_{M in T_a} [sum_{i!=j}psi(M_ij,F_ij)
                         +sum_i psi(M_ii,a_i)].         (3)

**Theorem.** A finite irreducible CTMC realizes the exact mean record,
with every hidden departure rate <=Lambda and each port departure rate
<=ell_i, if and only if (1) holds, T_a is nonempty, and

    2c >= J_cap.                                       (4)

Equality is attainable. This differs from the strict free-clock
criterion 2c>J_*. For V=0, c must be zero and the port budgets still
apply; the direct chain suffices. Off-diagonal rates may be zero.

The optimization is an ordinary finite linear program in an epigraph
representation. Since 0<=M_ij<=V, only finitely many lines in (2) can
be active for each positive fixed f. A separation implementation can
add just the line indexed by floor(Lambda*M_ij/f) at each candidate.
There is no claim of a new LP algorithm or cost-free numerical precision.
The fully expanded LP can have many lines when a flow is small; this
finite formulation alone is not a polynomial bit-complexity result.

# Independent review: directed mean-record realizability and state cost

29 October 2026. Ordinary proofs and exact controls for the root's oriented sufficient mean record. No statistical experiment or raw-data re-audit is performed. Here a positive CTMC means nonnegative transition rates and positive stationary weights; absent edges may have zero rate. Clocks are free design variables. An oriented record is not claimed minimal for scalar mean observations: time reversal can leave those observations unchanged.

## 1. Characterization

Let S be an irreducible m-port directed Laplacian with zero row and column sums, and F_ij=−S_ij>=0 for i≠j. Let w_B>0, v_R=b_R−w_B>=0, v_L=b_L−w_B>=0, with common total V>0. Let c>0. Let T be the transportation set of M>=0 with row sums v_R and column sums v_L, allowing every diagonal and only off-diagonals where F_ij>0. Define

    J*=min_{M in T} sum_{i!=j} M_ij²/F_ij.        (1)

The root's claim is sound: a finite irreducible CTMC realizes exactly (S,b_R,b_L,c,w_B) if and only if T is nonempty and 2c>J*. The strict inequality matters. Equality is a zero-variance limit, not a positive-duration finite CTMC realization.

## 2. Necessity and orientation

For an actual source, use positive invariant weights w and L=−diag(w)Q. Put C=L_II for hidden interior I and ρ_i=w_iλ_i. A trial departs port i and evolves natively to the next port J. Let σ be interior time after departure, zero for a direct port jump. Define

    Fall_ij=ρ_i Pr_i(J=j),
    M_ij=ρ_i E_i[σ 1_{J=j}].

The full flow Fall is balanced; its off-diagonals are F. Its diagonal return flows are not determined by S. The first excursion-moment matrix satisfies

    M=L_BI C^−1 diag(w_I) C^−1 L_IB.

It is entrywise nonnegative. Using C1=−L_IB1 and 1^TC=−1^TL_BI gives row(M)=v_R and column(M)=v_L. The second excursion moment gives

    sum_ij Fall_ij E_i[σ²|J=j]=2w_I^TC^−1w_I=2c. (2)

This identifies an acquisition distinction: in a nonreversible source, marginal duration means acquire v_R, whereas v_L generally requires duration jointly resolved by endpoint.

Every positive-M channel has a positive-duration component. A finite CTMC interior hold has nonzero conditional duration variance, even after conditioning on the terminal port; direct jumps only add a zero atom. Since V>0, conditional Jensen is strict for at least one channel. Therefore

    2c > sum_{ij:Fall_ij>0} M_
